A new study from researchers at NOAA’s National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) has uncovered a surprising number of coral species in the Pacific. And these are corals that have evolved to survive in low oxygen conditions—a phenomenon called “dead zones.” The study also shows how far away they can be found on coral reefs where there is no oxygen.
“As we monitor coral reef health throughout the year, we’re able to identify what corals are living on,” says Pamela Dahm, a marine biologist with NOAA’s Division of Marine Science, who was not involved in the study. “So if you go down to the reef and find corals living off-the-shelf coral reefs, you see that they get sick from too many toxins.”
The research is being published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Hydrology.
